acquisition method: The LTQ-Orbitrap Velos was operated in data-dependent acquisition mode with the XCalibur software.
alkylation reagent: Twenty µL of each of the resulting samples, corresponding to 9 different spiked levels of UPS1 (respectively 0.05–0.125–0.250–0.5–2.5–5–12.5–25–50 fmol of UPS1/µg of yeast lysate), were reduced with DTT and alkylated with iodoacetamide.
cleavage agent: The urea concentration was lowered to 1 M by dilution, and proteins were digested in solution by addition of 2% of trypsin overnight.
fragmentation method: The 20 most intense ions per survey scan were selected for CID fragmentation and the resulting fragments were analyzed in the linear trap (LTQ).
instrument: coupled to an LTQ-Orbitrap Velos mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Bremen, Germany).
ionization type: ESI-TRAP was chosen as the instrument, trypsin/P as the enzyme and 2 missed cleavages were allowed.
labeling: It can be used to objectively evaluate bioinformatic pipelines for label-free quantitative analysis, and their ability to detect variant proteins with good sensitivity and low false discovery rate in large-scale proteomic studies.
reduction reagent: Twenty µL of each of the resulting samples, corresponding to 9 different spiked levels of UPS1 (respectively 0.05–0.125–0.250–0.5–2.5–5–12.5–25–50 fmol of UPS1/µg of yeast lysate), were reduced with DTT and alkylated with iodoacetamide.
